article_title: A Meta-Analysis of Video Modeling Interventions for Children and Adolescents with Emotional/Behavioral Disorders
citation: Elias Clinton. (2016). A Meta-Analysis of Video Modeling Interventions for Children and Adolescents with Emotional/Behavioral Disorders. Educational Research Quarterly, 40(2). https://eric.ed.gov/?q=A+Meta-Analysis+of+Video+Modeling+Interventions+for+Children+and+Adolescents+with+Emotional%2FBehavioral+Disorders
title: Video modeling taxonomy: video modeling other (VMO) versus video self-modeling (VSM), grounded in Bandura's social learning theory
description: The article organizes video modeling interventions along one axis: VMO uses footage of an adult or peer (not the learner) engaging in a target behavior, while VSM uses "footage of the learner his/herself engaging in a target behavior in order to promote future occurrences of that target beh avior." VM applies Bandura's social learning theory, in which individuals learn skills through observation and vicarious reinforcement. The review indexes all 19 studies into these two categories and further classifies them by paired components, age, gender, and dependent measures.
requirements: Video footage of a model (other or self) engaging the target behavior, presented so the learner can observe and imitate it
constraints: Both variations have been found successful where other interventions have failed, per studies the review cites; the review does not rank VMO above VSM given the skewed study distribution
examples: The review classified 3 studies as VMO (e.g., Blood et al., 2011) and 16 as VSM (e.g., Clare, Jenson, Kehle, & Bray, 2000), with paired components including token economy, teacher feedback, and self-monitoring.
key_sources: Elias Clinton. (2016). A Meta-Analysis of Video Modeling Interventions for Children and Adolescents with Emotional/Behavioral Disorders. Educational Research Quarterly, 40(2). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1166705

article_title: Enriching Project-Based Learning Environments with Virtual Manipulatives: A Comparative Study
citation: Çakıroğlu, Ü. (2014). Enriching project-based learning environments with virtual manipulatives: A comparative study. Eurasian Journal of Educational Research, 55, 201-222. http://dx.doi.org/10.14689/ejer.2014.55.12
title: Repository of fifteen web-based virtual manipulatives for Polynomials and Quadratic Equations
description: A set of fifteen virtual manipulatives developed for the Polynomials (n=6) and Quadratic Equations (n=9) subjects of a 10th-grade mathematics curriculum, hosted on a website for use in ePBL projects. The article states that "The first step of the study was developing fifteen VMs related to the Polynomials (n=6) and Quadratic Equations (n=9) subjects". EG students used the VMs to gather information, manipulate parameters, and conduct experiments while solving project problems, while CG students were not aware of the repository.
requirements: Reviews by two mathematics education academicians and two mathematics teachers were taken to revise the VMs.
Both the quality and the quantity of VMs must be adequate.
constraints: In the study, only the EG students used the VMs; CG students completed projects using internet research, teachers' notes, and textbooks.
examples: Students could enter parameters related to operations on polynomials; one problem involved using algebra tiles in polynomials, and web records logged usage of each VM per project problem.
